newsitem.title: USA: Mother recovers children from father in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Mother recovers children from father in Lebanon.

text.p: A Florida woman was resuming life with her two children on Wednesday after retrieving them from Lebanon where they had been taken by their father three years ago during an angry separation and divorce.
Nabela Henry arrived at Miami International Airport late Tuesday holding tightly the hands of her son Ramzy, 7, and daughter, Nora, 5, after reaching U.S. soil.

Her journey began on Friday in Miami, and went through Vienna, Cyprus and Beirut before she retrieved the children in Tripoli, and then travelled back through Paris, Geneva and New York before reaching Miami.

"It's a miracle case. You just don't get in and out of that country like that," said Mark Miller, founder of the Houston-based, non-profit American Association for Lost Children, which helped Henry get her children back.

Henry's reunion with the children at their school in Tripoli on Monday had marked the first time she had seen them since Oct. 31, 1993. The children's father, Saad Abdo, fled the country with them after taking them for what was supposed to have been a weekend visit.

Henry, Miller and another investigator from the association had found the children's school after staking out Abdo's house and making inquiries in Tripoli. They had known only that the children were attending an American private school.
Henry said both children recognised her immediately, even though Nora had been only 2-1/2 when she had last seen her mother. They had spoken on the phone occasionally during the separation.

"When I picked her up, and I said, 'Nora, this is Mommy. She just hugged me, and was smiling,'" she said. "I asked her, 'How do you know I'm your mommy?' I asked her, and she said, 'I know, because I remember.'"
"I'm happy. It's very exciting," Henry said.

Police in her hometown North Lauderdale, Florida, had told Henry they could not help her because the children's disappearance was not a kidnapping. She also said the U.S. government had not helped. The couple was separated but not yet divorced when the children were taken, so Abdo had joint custody.
She received a divorce decree and custody in 1994, but Abdo refused to send her the children or even tell her where they were.
